title: Questions 2 (do you know where … ? / he asked me where …)

exercises.instruction: Which is right? Tick (✓) the correct alternative.

options: a Do you know what time the film starts?
b Do you know what time does the film start?
c Do you know what time starts the film?
a Why Amy does get up so early every day?
b Why Amy gets up so early every day?
c Why does Amy get up so early every day?
a I want to know what this word means.
b I want to know what does this word mean.
c I want to know what means this word.
a I can't remember where did I park the car.
b I can't remember where I parked the car.
c I can't remember where I did park the car.
a Why you didn't phone me yesterday?
b Why didn't you phone me yesterday?
c Why you not phoned me yesterday?
a Do you know where does Helen work?
b Do you know where Helen does work?
c Do you know where Helen works?
a How much it costs to park here?
b How much does it cost to park here?
c How much it does cost to park here?
a Tell me what you want.
b Tell me what you do want.
c Tell me what do you want.

exercises.instruction: Put the words in the correct order.

answers: Do you know what time it is?
How far is it to the airport?
I wonder how old Tom is.
How long have they been married?

items.prompt: (they / married / how long / been / have / know)
answers: Do you know how long they have been married?

items.prompt: (tell / the station / you / me / is / where)
answers: Could you tell me where the station is?

items.prompt: (in the accident / injured / anyone / don't / whether / know / was)
answers: I don't know whether anyone was injured in the accident.

items.prompt: (what / tomorrow / know / time / will / arrive / you / you)
answers: Do you know what time you will arrive tomorrow?

exercises.instruction: You were visiting London. You met a lot of people who asked you a lot of questions. Now you tell a friend what people asked you. Use reported speech.

answers: He asked me where I was from.

items.prompt: (How long have you been in London?)
answers: She asked me how long I'd been in London.
She asked me how long I had been in London.
They asked me if I'd been to London before.
They asked me if I had been to London before.
They asked me whether I'd been to London before.
They asked me whether I had been to London before.
She asked me if I liked London.
She asked me whether I liked London.
He asked me where I was staying.

items.prompt: (How long are you going to stay?)
answers: She asked me how long I was going to stay.
She asked me if I thought London was expensive.
She asked me if I thought London is expensive.
She asked me whether I thought London was expensive.
She asked me whether I thought London is expensive.
They asked me why I'd come to London.
They asked me why I had come to London.
They asked me why I came to London.
